name: Skift Research: AI in Travel Discovery, Search and Revenue Management
title: Skift Research: AI in Travel Discovery, Search and Revenue Management
answer: Skift Research is the research arm of the travel-industry news organisation Skift, publishing reports on how AI is reshaping travel. Its most useful single finding for hospitality readers is that AI now accounts for 21% of touchpoints at the inspiration stage of the booking journey but only 6% at booking, and that 63% of travellers prefer a curated shortlist over a single AI-chosen itinerary.

sections.body: Skift Research is the research division of Skift, the travel-industry news and intelligence company, and its site at research.skift.com carries report pages, an archive of past reports, and a homepage describing its subscription offerings. The reports examined here cover AI in travel discovery, Google's AI Overviews in travel search, generative AI's impact on travel, and AI in airline revenue management. The site also carries a 2017 article introducing Skift Research, which notes the team then numbered five people and that the service was in its fourth year of publication. The homepage states that Skift now runs on Skift Intelligence, a subscription layer updated daily.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The report on travel discovery, produced with McKinsey & Company and drawing on a survey of more than 1,000 U.S. travellers plus a large language model destination study, maps where AI appears across the booking journey and finds that it personalises the pitch for a traveller type more than it changes the underlying destination list. A companion report on Google's AI Overviews describes their visibility for travel searches quadrupling over six months and concentrating attention on a small number of established travel sites, which challenges traditional SEO and paid marketing. A third report estimates generative AI poses a $28 billion-plus opportunity for travel and examines seven use cases spanning chatbots, operational efficiency and search, with four baseline areas of immediate impact and three longer-term disruption opportunities. A fourth covers AI in airline revenue management, noting executive hesitation because small errors in complex airline systems can cause system-wide breakdowns, and covering modern distribution strategy, advanced pricing models and the market opportunity AI creates in that function.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: Skift Research reports that AI accounts for 21% of touchpoints at the inspiration stage, 16% at research, 6% at booking and 29% after booking. Travellers are roughly twice as comfortable using AI for ideas and comparisons (40% and 50%) as for booking (27%), and 63% prefer a curated shortlist over an unfiltered catalog or a single AI-chosen itinerary. The top five destinations drew 38% of all recommendations and the top 10 drew 48%, while 29% of persona-destination pairs rated a high fit were never recommended. Google's AI Overviews quadrupled in travel-search visibility over six months. Generative AI is put at a $28 billion-plus opportunity for travel. The homepage cites June 11, 2026 signals: OTA commission fees at 22 to 28%, mid-scale RevPAR projected down 4.7% against a Q3 2025 baseline, and metasearch click-through down 31% in tested markets where AI Overviews surface hotel prices directly.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: For anyone following AI in hospitality, this source supplies measured evidence rather than vendor claims. The discovery research quantifies where AI already intervenes in the booking journey and shows that recommendation engines narrow destination choice, which matters to hotels and destinations competing for an AI-generated shortlist. The search report explains why visibility is consolidating around established sites as AI Overviews expand, with a direct commercial consequence in the 31% metasearch click-through decline cited on the homepage. The generative AI report sizes the opportunity and separates near-term from long-term use cases, and the airline revenue management report documents why operators in complex systems hesitate to adopt AI. Together these give hotel, airline and OTA strategists benchmarks for planning.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Hospitality

sections.body: The findings here come from report landing pages and archive listings rather than the full reports, so methodology and sample detail are only partly visible, and several figures appear as homepage signals dated June 11, 2026 without fuller sourcing on the pages read. The material is commercial: Skift Research sells subscriptions, and the homepage describes pricing customised by team size and deployment, with Skift Intelligence included in every subscription. Coverage is travel-wide rather than hospitality-specific, spanning airlines, OTAs, destinations and short-term rentals, so hotel readers must judge relevance themselves. The 2017 article is dated and describes the organisation as it then stood.
